title: The Silver Toll
hook: The old toll collector left one rule: if anyone pays with a silver dollar, lift the gate... and don't look inside the car.
lines: I work nights in the last toll booth before the mountain pass.
The old collector, Gus, left me one rule, taped above the coin tray.
If anyone pays with a silver dollar... lift the gate. And don't look inside the car.
For a month, it was only truckers, fog, and the hum of my little heater.
Then, at three a.m., a long gray station wagon rolled up. Headlights off.
The window cranked down. A hand, white as frost, dropped a silver dollar in my tray.
I kept my eyes on the coin. I lifted the gate.
But as it rolled past... I glanced at the back windows.
Faces. Pale and still. Every one of them pressed to the glass... watching me.
And in the last seat, I saw Gus. The man who quit without saying goodbye.
Last night, that wagon came back... and Gus was the one driving.
He opened the back door... and patted the empty seat.
